classification.difficultyReason: Represent the unknown remainder as a linear polynomial, translate the two given remainders into its values at distinct symbolic roots, and solve symbolically for its coefficients using a≠b.

content.prompt: Let $P(x)$ be a polynomial leaving remainder $A$ when divided by $(x-a)$, and remainder $B$ when divided by $(x-b)$, where $a\ne b$. Find the remainder when $P(x)$ is divided by $(x-a)(x-b)$.

answer.short:
$\displaystyle \frac{A-B}{a-b}x+\frac{aB-bA}{a-b}$.

Write the remainder as $mx+c$, substitute $x=a$ and $x=b$, and solve simultaneously.
answer.worked:
The divisor has degree 2, so write the remainder as $R(x)=mx+c$. The division identity is
$$P(x)=(x-a)(x-b)Q(x)+mx+c.$$
By the remainder theorem, $P(a)=A$ and $P(b)=B$. Substitution gives
$$\begin{align*}ma+c&=A\\mb+c&=B.\end{align*}$$
Subtracting these equations and using $a\ne b$,
$$\begin{align*}m(a-b)&=A-B\\m&=\frac{A-B}{a-b}.\end{align*}$$
Substitute into $ma+c=A$:
$$\begin{align*}c&=A-\frac{a(A-B)}{a-b}\\c&=\frac{aB-bA}{a-b}.\end{align*}$$
Therefore the remainder is
$$R(x)=\frac{A-B}{a-b}x+\frac{aB-bA}{a-b}.$$
